sections.h2: What written or spoken notice must a Georgia landlord give before an eviction?
sections.html:
A Georgia landlord must first demand that the tenant give up the home, and for unpaid rent the landlord must also hand over a written pay-or-quit notice at least three business days before going to court. The Georgia Landlord-Tenant Handbook from the Department of Community Affairs says the demand itself can be spoken unless rent is the reason, and that no particular wording is required.

A spoken demand is hard to prove later, so the handbook tells landlords to keep a record of when and how they delivered it. The sample it offers is dated, names the tenant and the address, lists the lease term that was broken, and sets a number of days to leave. Whatever the lease says about notice or termination also has to be followed, which makes the lease the first paper to pull out for a landlord or a tenant.

  • The tenant's name and the rental address
  • The date of the notice and the way it was delivered
  • The lease term that was violated, or the rent and fees owed
  • The number of days the tenant has to surrender the home

sections.h2: How does the three business day rent notice work?
sections.html:
The landlord serves a written demand for the back rent and fees, and three business days must pass before a dispossessory case can be filed over money. The handbook says the notice can go out by any method named in the lease, or it can be posted on the unit door in a sealed envelope.

The court affidavit that follows has to say the landlord demanded possession and was refused, and where rent is the reason it has to confirm the three day notice was given. After service of the case papers, the tenant has seven days to pay what the affidavit claims plus court costs. Paying in full ends the case, but the handbook limits this tender defense to once in any twelve month period with the same landlord.

Once a rent case is filed, a landlord normally stops accepting rent so that no payment can be used as a defense. If the case runs longer than two weeks, the landlord can ask the court to order the tenant to pay rent into the court registry while it waits.

sections.h2: How many days does a month-to-month tenancy need to end?
sections.html:
A landlord ending a tenancy at will must give sixty days of notice, and a tenant ending one must give thirty days. The same sixty days applies when a landlord wants to keep the tenant but change the rent amount, since that starts a new tenancy at will.

The handbook also explains how a fixed lease turns into this arrangement. If a lease runs out, the tenant stays, and the landlord keeps taking monthly rent, a tenancy at will arises on the old lease terms, and the sixty and thirty day rules then control. A private landlord does not have to give a reason for declining to renew unless the lease requires one, as long as no discrimination law is broken.

There is a narrow exception on the tenant side. A tenant who holds a court order protecting them or their minor children in a family violence or stalking situation may end a lease on thirty days of notice.

sections.h2: Which Georgia eviction notice or deadline fits each situation?
sections.html:
Georgia landlord and tenant timing as printed in the DCA Landlord-Tenant Handbook (revised 8-29-24) and the Georgia Courts self-help page
SituationNotice or deadlineWho acts
Unpaid rent or feesWritten notice, then three business days before filingLandlord
Other lease violation or holdoverDemand for possession, spoken or writtenLandlord
Ending a tenancy at willSixty daysLandlord
Leaving a tenancy at willThirty daysTenant
Answering the court papersSeven days from actual serviceTenant
Paying rent and costs to stop the caseSeven days after serviceTenant
Moving after a ruling for the landlordWrit requires the tenant to move after seven daysCourt and sheriff

sections.h2: What happens after the notice period ends?
sections.html:
The landlord files a sworn dispossessory affidavit, usually in magistrate court in the county where the rental sits, and the papers are served on the tenant. In most counties the sheriff serves them by handing them to the tenant, giving them to an adult living in the home, or tacking a copy on the door and mailing one.

The tenant then has seven days from actual service to answer, and the clerk will take the answer orally or in writing. When the seventh day lands on a weekend or legal holiday the deadline moves to the next business day. If no answer comes, the court can order the tenant out and send the sheriff, and a default judgment cannot be appealed. Where an answer raises a valid defense, a hearing is usually set within about seven days.

A ruling for the landlord leads to a writ of possession, which is a separate document from the order. The sheriff generally supervises the removal, and the landlord pays for it.

sections.h2: Can a Georgia landlord skip the notice and change the locks?
sections.html:
No. Georgia Courts and the handbook both say a landlord cannot remove a tenant or block access without going through the court process, even when rent is unpaid. A tenant is entitled to stay with active utilities until the court decides.

Georgia also presumes retaliation when a landlord files for eviction, raises rent, cuts services or ends a lease within three months after a tenant asks for repairs, reports a code violation, or takes part in a tenant group. A landlord can rebut that with a lawful reason such as unpaid rent, serious misconduct or a holdover. A tenant who wins a retaliation claim may recover one month of rent plus $500, court costs and possibly attorney fees.

sections.h2: How does an eviction notice affect selling a Georgia house?
sections.html:
It adds steps that a buyer, the owner and the court clerk all need to track, so find out where the case stands before you sign a contract. Ask the magistrate court clerk in the county where the house sits whether a dispossessory case is open, and ask a Georgia attorney whether the lease continues after a sale.

The handbook covers one sale rule: when someone new buys a rental, the former owner must either move the security deposit to the new owner or refund it to the tenant. A tenant who is owed the deposit can sue if neither happens. A person who never had the owner's permission to be on the property is treated differently. The handbook describes that person as a squatter, and an owner can swear an affidavit to have a squatter removed without an eviction case.

Georgia is also a state of homeowners. The Census Bureau lists 11,302,748 residents as of July 1, 2025, an owner-occupied housing rate of 65.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, and a median gross rent of $1,393 for the same years. Rented houses are a real share of what changes hands here, so an as-is buyer should be asked in writing whether the house will be taken with the tenant in place.

faqs.q: Does a Georgia landlord have to give written notice before evicting?
faqs.a: Only in the rent case. The handbook says a demand to leave can be spoken for most reasons, but a landlord must give written notice to pay at least three business days before filing over unpaid rent or fees. Because a spoken demand is hard to prove, a dated paper copy protects both sides.

faqs.q: How much notice does a month-to-month tenant get in Georgia?
faqs.a: Sixty days. A landlord ending a tenancy at will gives sixty days, and a tenant leaving gives thirty days. The sixty day period also applies to a landlord who wants to change the rent on a month-to-month tenant.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to respond once court papers arrive?
faqs.a: Seven days from actual service. A tenant who misses that window can lose by default, and a default judgment cannot be appealed. If the seventh day is a weekend or holiday, the answer is due the next business day.

faqs.q: Can a tenant stop an eviction for unpaid rent by paying?
faqs.a: Yes, once. Paying everything the affidavit claims plus court costs within seven days of service is a complete defense, but a tenant can use it only one time in twelve months with the same landlord. The tenant should also file an answer saying the money was paid or offered.

faqs.q: Does selling the house cancel an eviction notice in Georgia?
faqs.a: Nothing in the handbook says a sale cancels a notice or a lease. It does say the old owner must transfer the security deposit or refund it. Ask the county magistrate court clerk about any open case and consult a Georgia attorney about the lease before closing.
